KINA follows a CIP-aligned taxonomy refined into 12 top-level disciplines, 70 fields, and 261 fine-grained subfields.
The dataset contains 899 ten-option pseudo-multiple-choice questions covering 261 fine-grained subfields, 70 fields, and 12 top-level disciplines .
Pseudo-multiple-choice structure: many items contain multiple foundational statements in the stem, and each option corresponds to a combinatorial judgment over those statements.
Source grounding: claims should be traceable to authoritative sources, such as peer-reviewed journals, monographs, textbooks, official databases, or rigorously cited academic materials.

KINA rejects questions whose difficulty comes mainly from narrow rote memory, ambiguous wording, semantic traps, volatile scholarly opinion, or hidden context such as "in this paper" or "in the attachment" without the required premises.
Two independent reviewers score each item for representativeness/depth, factuality, source reliability, logical rigor, distractor plausibility, and combinatorial validity.
Annotators and reviewers were recruited from graduate students at top-tier global universities and senior industry experts.
Pairwise model gaps below roughly 2 percentage points may not be statistically distinguishable at the 95% level in the current 899-item release.

The 3-of-5 flagship-model failure filter ties the difficulty distribution to the model landscape available during dataset construction, so KINA will require periodic refreshes as frontier models improve.
KINA is an evaluation benchmark and should not be used as a substitute for professional certification, expert review, or safety evaluation in high-stakes settings.
The paper evaluation uses AVG@4 accuracy with default temperature, a 32K maximum output budget, and a 16K reasoning budget or the model provider's medium reasoning setting where applicable.
Web-search augmentation is positive but non-uniform across the evaluated tool-use cohort, ranging from +1.50 to +5.17 points.
